# The verdict page, rebuilt off the honest book, and the staleness trap fixed

**2026-08-30.** `research/omen-71-verdict.html` is regenerated by `research/g82_artifact_cleanup_build.py`,
which now reads its numbers live off `research/bt2y_trades.json` (the honest close-fill book,
`research/g85_honest_book.md`) instead of the dated `research/t23_stack.json` snapshot it used to
hard-read with no freshness check.

## The two problems, fixed

**1. The staleness trap.** The old generator opened `research/t23_stack.json` — a 29-August file —
and printed whatever was in it, with nothing checking that file still matched the book on disk. It
was still printing **2,437 trades and $1,339,000** after the book had been rebuilt twice underneath
it (dedupe fix → 4,508 trades, then the honest-fill rebuild → 4,329 trades). That is the exact bug
`research/book_stamp.py` exists to catch, one level up from where it was first found.

The new generator:
- Reads every dollar and R figure **live** off `research/bt2y_trades.json` and
  `research/bt2y_trades_published_fill.json` via `book_stamp.book_figures()`, which re-parses
  whenever the file's mtime changes — not off any cached intermediate JSON.
- **Asserts** the live book's identity — fill, trade count, signal count, sha256 `book_id` —
  against the constants the generator was written against
  (`book_stamp.assert_book`), and separately checks the recall report
  (`research/g85_recall_honest.json`) was built the same day as the book. Any mismatch raises
  and the script refuses to write the page, rather than print a stale number. Verified live:

  ```
  $ python -c "... EXPECT_BOOK['traded']=2437; load_figures() ..."
  FAILED LOUDLY (expected, BookMismatch):
  C:\...\bt2y_trades.json is not the book these figures came from:
    traded: published 2437, book on disk has 4329
  ```
- Prints the fill mode and the book's build commit **on the page itself** — a provenance line
  under the header (`book bt2y_trades.json · fill CLOSE · commit 3dfb0865 · id f76361ae47e9a3b2 ·
  built 2026-08-30T10:59:54`) and again in the footer.

**2. Google Fonts.** Removed both `<link rel="preconnect">` tags and the `fonts.googleapis.com`
stylesheet. The three font roles now resolve to system stacks: sans → `system-ui, -apple-system,
"Segoe UI", Roboto, ...`, mono → `ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", "SFMono-Regular", Consolas, ...`,
serif display → `Georgia, "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", "Book Antiqua", serif`. No other
CSS token changed — `research/g83_dark_theme.md` had already audited this page's dark palette as
spec-correct (light-on-`:root`, overridden under both the media query and `[data-theme="dark"]`,
explicit `body{background:var(--bg)}`), so the color system was left untouched.

## What else the task asked for

- **The $397/day bar is now an explicit line on the page** — a callout directly under the three
  gate cards: "$397 / day — Austin's money bar, ratified 2026-08-30 ... Every dollar figure on
  this page is measured against this line," plus a second paragraph explaining what "NOT
  OBTAINABLE" means wherever it appears.
- **The published-fill control is labeled `NOT OBTAINABLE`** (a small red pill, reusing the
  existing `.pill.miss` component — no new CSS) everywhere it appears: all three gate cards, the
  "what moved" table header, the bar-line callout, and the footer.
- **Format unchanged.** Same masthead → gates → bar line → what-moved table → still-blocking →
  actions → not-run → footer structure, same CSS component set (gate cards, pills, `.callout`,
  `.scroll` table, `ol.acts`). Nothing was redesigned; only data, labels, and fonts.

## Old vs. new: the numbers that changed

| | old page (T23 stack, 29 Aug) | **new page (honest book, 30 Aug)** |
|---|---:|---:|
| Money gate | +0.5495R (target 2.0R, was +0.8341R) | **$28/day = +0.0278R, one trade a day** (target $397/day · all signals −$283/day, −0.0327R · was $721/day published fill, **NOT OBTAINABLE**) |
| Durability gate | 25 / 25 (target every month, was 23/25) | **11 / 25**, one trade a day (all signals: 8/25 · was 25/25 published fill, **NOT OBTAINABLE** — MET, but unobtainable) |
| Recall gate | 67.6% (target 90%, was 52.9% — wrong-router note) | **74.3%** of his S days (target ≥90%, 15.7 pts short · was 59.1% published fill · router bug now fixed, gain is more firing not better sorting) |
| Traded signals (footer) | 2,437 | **4,329** honest / 4,508 on the frozen published-fill control |
| Signals detected (footer) | 76,019 | **127,188** |
| Fonts | Google Fonts (Instrument Serif, IBM Plex Sans/Mono) | system font stacks, no external request |
| "What moved" table | T0 book vs T23 stack (12,437-trade era) | **published fill vs. honest fill**, 12 rows, both policies (one-a-day and all-signals) |

Every number above traces to `research/g85_honest_book.md` / `.json` (money, durability, trade
and signal counts) and `research/g85_recall_honest.md` / `.json` (recall), both dated 2026-08-30,
both re-derivable offline with no backtest re-run.

## What I deliberately left alone, and why

The **"What is still blocking"**, **"What you can do"**, and **"What did not run"** sections are
independent research findings authored as static prose — the generator never derived them from
any book, before or after this rewrite. Rewriting all fourteen items against the honest book would
mean re-running or re-verifying analyses (the min-viable-stop guard, the exit-arm sweep, the
disaster-stop A/B, the arrival-order and loss-halt measurements, the level-count and card-filter
checks) that this task did not ask for and that I have not re-run. Doing that silently would repeat
the exact failure this task exists to fix, at a different layer.

Instead:
- **"Still blocking" item 1 was corrected**, because it was flatly wrong, not just dated: it
  described the recall harness as measuring the wrong router. That bug was fixed 2026-08-29 (G72,
  see `DIRECTION.md`). The item now states the current, real finding — recall is 74.3% on the
  honest fill, but the gain is bought by trading more days (false fires +16.9 pts), not by sorting
  them better (`research/g85_recall_honest.md`).
- **Items 2 and 3 of "still blocking," and all eleven action items, are unchanged in substance**
  but the action-list intro and a new "What did not run" bullet both say plainly that they were
  computed on the published fill (now labeled NOT OBTAINABLE throughout) and have not been
  re-verified against the honest book — the underlying questions may still stand; the R-multiples
  and dollar figures attached to them may not.
- **The disaster-stop action item (#2) gained one clarifying sentence** from tonight's stops
  finding (`research/g82_stop_ab.md`): the code has never actually run the close-only version of
  the rule it asks about, because the disaster stop is tested on a touch, first, at the same price
  as the level stop.

untouched, per `research/g83_dark_theme.md`'s prior audit of this exact page).
